title: Traveling-wave MZM EO bandwidth
description: Electro-optic bandwidth of the traveling-wave MZM (models/optical_power/mzm_tw.va) as a network-analyser AC sweep: LAS1 holds the optical input CW, the model biases the electrode at quadrature (vbias=vpi/2), VE drives the electrode with a 1 V AC tone and PD detects the optical output. AC mode measures H(f) = v(out_eo) per volt of electrode drive — the modulator's small-signal EO response. On top of the quasi-static cos() transfer, mzm_tw imposes the two effects that set a real TW electrode's EO bandwidth: frequency-dependent electrode loss (pole at f_el = 35 GHz) and optical/RF velocity walk-off (pole at 0.443*c/(|n_rf-n_opt|*len) ~ 18 GHz for the default n_rf=2.4 vs n_opt=4.2 electrode). Their cascade gives an EO -3 dB bandwidth of ~15 GHz. Set MZM.n_rf = 4.2 (velocity-matched) and re-run: the walk-off pole vanishes, only f_el limits, and the -3 dB pushes out toward the electrode-loss corner. The pinned physics study is examples/mzm_tw_eo_bw.py (the same |H(f)| sweep, checked against the analytic pole cascade).
